answer: Proof-of-space minting resists sybils: each identity must dedicate a large, unique region of physical storage and continuously answer unpredictable challenges that mirror random offsets of it, proving the bytes are really held. A vine of a thousand fakes needs a thousand distinct terabytes physically allocated — storage cannot be shared or spiral-compressed away, since the probes hit random positions a deduplicated copy could not answer for every identity at once. Honest agents commit one region; a farm's cost grows linearly per head in real disk, the scarce resource proof-of-space prices.
